title: Oryx private deploy - weekly unblock + 1:1 prep (Izzy)
content:
Purpose / quick scope
- Notes for weekly sync with Oryx team (customer) + internal 1:1 with Ravi. Focus: remove infra blockers that are preventing canary (stage) rollout of private deployment into customer VPC.
- This is a personal scratchpad for prep and follow-ups; will copy relevant bits to Confluence and the weekly email.

Participants (planned)
- Oryx: Lina Park (Infra Lead), Marco Ruiz (Security), Kelsey (App PM)
- Redwood: Isabel Carter (SE, owner), Ravi Menon (Infra eng), Hannah Lee (SRE), Dmitri Volkov (Network specialist)

Top agenda items (30m)
1) Quick status (3m): where canary is blocked today
2) VPC peering / routing glitch (8m): review traceroutes and security group rules, next steps to validate egress path
3) KMS/HSM integration update (5m): Marco's PKI timeline and RW KMS cert rotation plan
4) Node sizing and GPU capacity (5m): confirm final nodepool sizes and readiness for quantization workloads
5) Smoke test checklist + acceptance criteria (6m): agree on pass threshold for canary and who signs off

My talking points / lines to probe
- "We need one reliable success path for traffic from Oryx app to Redwood inference endpoint (VPC private link or NAT + egress list). Which of those is operationally preferred for you?"
- Ask Lina if there are any additional security scanners or NIDS that will drop long-lived TLS sessions (we've seen sessions reset with certain IDS configs).
- Emphasize rollback plan: if canary fails, we will switch traffic to hosted endpoint for 30m while we fix the private route. Need acceptance from Kelsey.

Current blockers (explicit)
- B1: Asymmetric routing when traffic exits customer subnet -> packet returns via transit gateway (observed traceroute mismatch). Owner: Dmitri. Impact: intermittent token errors during streaming.
- B2: KMS key policy doesn't allow Redwood service principal to wrap/unwrap keys for staged env. Owner: Marco. Impact: can't start encrypted model artifacts download.
- B3: Helm chart v2.7.1 crashloop on init for model-cache sidecar (race with EBS mount). Owner: Ravi. Impact: pod fails to reach Ready state, prevents canary pods.
- B4: Acceptance metrics not instrumented in customer's observability (they only send app logs, no per-request latency). Owner: Hannah (work with customer). Impact: cannot auto-promote.

Desired outcomes for this sync
- Dmitri proposes 2 mitigations for B1 by next Thu (2026-03-12): a quick route policy we can test + a longer-term TGW route-table change.
- Marco confirms KMS policy change approved and scheduled by Fri 2026-03-06 with exact policy snippet we can test with a dev key.
- Ravi owns a hotfix to the Helm chart and will open PR + test on dev cluster by Tue 2026-03-03.
- Hannah will pair with Oryx telemetry lead to add 3 metrics (request_count, p95_latency, error_rate) to their Prometheus scrape by Mon 2026-03-08.

Action items (my personal follow-ups)
- A1: Draft short email to Kelsey summarizing rollback steps and request for sign-off window (deadline: today EOD).
- A2: Run targeted traceroute with Dmitri and record outputs (task: run from Oryx app pod and from Redwood nat instance). Attach results to JIRA-INF-4871. (deadline: 2026-03-03)
- A3: Validate KMS policy once Marco posts snippet; try wrap/unwrap with staging key; if fails, request temporary provisioning of a test key. (deadline: 2026-03-06)
- A4: Test Helm hotfix locally and push comments on PR #89; coordinate with Ravi for follow-up smoke run. (deadline: 2026-03-04)
- A5: Write minimal smoke checklist for canary (<=10 steps) and share in channel #oryx-vpc. (deadline: 2026-03-02)

Notes to self (scratch)
- When doing smoke checklist, prioritize: TLS handshake success, model artifact fetch OK, initial tokenized generation < 300ms for p50, no OOMs in logs, persistent KV cache mount.
- Remember to ask whether Oryx will enable flow logs for the subnet; that would help B1 debugging (they're cautious about cost).
- If KMS rotation window is constrained (only nightly), propose a short maintenance window with Canary traffic diverted to hosted for 20m.

Open questions to raise
- Q1: Can Oryx provide a short-lived VPN jumpbox we can SSH into during the session for live debugging? (quick wins often come from running tcpdump).
- Q2: Do they have a hard limit on ephemeral outbound connections (some customers cap port ranges)?
- Q3: Are there existing egress proxy rules that could be rewriting SNI or TLS headers for inspection?

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Long traceroute asymmetry causes intermittent failures during streaming and we only see it under load.
  Mitigation: Run sustained lightweight load test (50 concurrent sessions) in staging before canary; if flakiness appears, fallback to NAT path for the canary with stricter circuit breaker thresholds.
- Risk: Helm fix changes volume mount timing and could surface on prod nodes with different disk speed.
  Mitigation: Include a step in smoke tests to read/write small files to volume at init and measure latency.

Prep checklist for 1:1 with Ravi (10m)
- Confirm status of Helm fix and whether PR blocks on integration tests. Ask if he needs access to a perf node for reproduce.
- Confirm who will run the dev-key KMS validation. Offer to run it if Ravi can drop credentials in vault.
- Agree on time to jointly observe a canary run (tentative: 2026-03-09 10:00 PT).

Copy snippets (to paste into sync)
- Short ask to Oryx for the sync: "Goal for today: unblock canary. We need agreement on route test and a window for KMS policy change. Expect ~20-30m sync. Please have Lina/Dmitri + Marco available if possible."

Follow-up template (post-meeting)
- Quick subject: Oryx private deploy — sync notes & action items [date]
- 1-2 line summary of what we agreed, list of action items with owners + due dates, links to artifacts (Jira/PR), next touchpoint date/time.

Random thoughts / future improvements (brain dump)
- Would be great to add a small Redwood diagnostic container we can request Oryx to run in their infrastructure: it would run traceroute, curl to endpoints with different source ports, perform TLS handshakes and report NAT translations. Minimal permissions only. Could be a standard ask for future private deployments.
- Consider adding a toggle in our helm chart to wait-for-volume-with-timeout to make mounts more deterministic across different disk speeds.

End of scratchpad. Will trim and move to Confluence after sync.
